comparison.objective: Disinfect an IV connector hub for 15 seconds, then seat a syringe and complete a measured saline flush; the candidate instead sets and locks a robot gripper opening stop and verifies retained articulation.
comparison.physical_skill: PR-1013 tests sustained frictional wiping, contamination-aware sequencing, coaxial syringe seating, and plunger actuation. It does not test concentric screw/jam-nut counterholding, preservation of an angular adjustment under locking torque, or post-lock mechanism cycling.
comparison.success_condition: PR-1013 requires 300 valid scrub samples, no premature syringe contact, aligned seating, and ultimately at least 5 mL discharged with at least 4.5 mL collected; partial scores distinguish cleaning, seating, and flushing. The candidate requires a released 90° opening within tolerance, seated/retained nuts, three repeat cycles with limited drift, tool withdrawal, and one-second clearance. No material rubric details are missing from the available versions.
comparison.reason: The tasks share fine alignment and tool handling only at a generic level; infection-control wiping and fluid-line access do not exercise the candidate's defining ability to preserve a mechanical stop while locking it against reaction torque and validate retained motion.
